content: The test image shows a collapsed/dead seedling at soil level — the stem has rotted and the plant has fallen over, with surrounding healthy green seedlings. This is classic damping-off symptom. Top candidates: **Pythium_damping_off** and **Rhizoctonia**.

Neither SCN nor Brown Stem Rot match — those show mature plant symptoms. Returning to my key candidates.

**Visual analysis summary:**
- Young seedling completely collapsed and dead at soil level
- Sandy, light-colored dry soil
- Surrounding seedlings are healthy and small (early establishment stage)
- The affected plant has a yellowed/browned appearance, fallen over

**Differentiation:**
- **Pythium_damping_off**: Reference shows very early seedlings (cotyledon stage) on wet, dark clay soil with water-soaked soft rot — doesn't match the dry sandy environment
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reference bottom-right panel shows seedlings collapsed at soil line in sandy soil conditions — matches closely
- Phytophthora, Fusarium, SDS, BSR all show mature plant symptoms — ruled out

The dry sandy soil and collapsed seedling pattern best match **Rhizoctonia**, which can cause pre- and post-emergence damping off in drier conditions with a reddish-brown hypocotyl lesion causing the plant to fall over.
